The test image shows a corn ear with:
- Husks pulled back revealing the cob
- Pink/white fungal mycelium covering much of the ear
- Brown rotted tip with dark fungal mass
- Kernel discoloration (pink/red tones)
- Rot progressing from the tip inward

This pattern strongly suggests Gibberella ear rot — pink mold starting at the tip is classic. Let me verify with one reference image.

The reference matches well — both show discolored kernels (pink/brown tones) with white fungal mycelium on a corn ear. The test image shows more pronounced tip rot with dense fungal growth, which is characteristic of Gibberella ear rot progressing from the tip downward.
